prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures the downward-angled layout over a slanted concrete ground plane that recedes smoothly from about 1.3 m at the bottom foreground to 3–5 m at the top edge across all five frames. In frames 1 to 4, the brightest regions at the bottom center correspond to the camera wearer's own torso, right hand (0.3–0.6 m away, within arm's reach), and legs/feet (1.0–1.5 m below the camera), with a faint slightly brighter silhouette on the floor in frames 3 and 4 marking the skateboard about 0.2–0.4 m in front of the wearer's feet (~1.5 m from the camera). In frame 5, as the camera turns right and a second person enters on the left within arm's reach (0.6–1.4 m from the camera wearer and ~0.8 m to the left of the wearer's feet), the depth map highlights the second person's torso and arm as a bright white foreground mass while the wearer's own feet and skateboard shift to the bottom right. Compared to the dark, low-contrast RGB image, the depth map makes the continuous tilt of the ground plane and the close proximity of the second person's upper body vs. the floor immediately clear. However, the map is unreliable for thin or dark floor objects and distant background structure, nearly blending the black skateboard into the ground in frames 1–3, saturating the top edge to black, and merging the second person's feet with the floor in frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates foreground people and objects against a black background across the flat concrete scene, consistently segmenting the camera wearer's lower body, torso, and right arm at the bottom center of frames 1–4 (0.3–1.5 m below the camera) and bottom right of frame 5 as a 'person' mask. In frames 1 and 2, the skateboard on the ground is occluded by the wearer's right leg and completely missed, whereas in frame 4 the skateboard (~1.5 m away, just in front of the wearer's feet) is segmented as a distinct pink mask above the wearer's feet. In frame 5, as the second person approaches on the left within arm's reach (0.6–1.4 m away, ~0.8 m left of the wearer's feet, facing forward/right away from the camera with their head and shoulders cropped out of the left frame edge), the map separates the second person's torso/arm on the left from the camera wearer's legs on the bottom right. This map makes the exact boundary between the wearer's legs and the skateboard in frame 4 and between the two people in frame 5 easier to distinguish than in the dim RGB frames. However, it is highly unreliable in semantics and completeness: it mislabels the skateboard as 'airplane' in frame 4, misses the skateboard in frames 1–3 and 5, fails to segment the ground plane, and hallucinates a fragmented 'person' mask on the distant upper-left skatepark background (~4–6 m away) in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the five frames, detecting only a single magenta hand skeleton in the bottom center of frame 3 corresponding to the camera wearer's right hand (~0.5 m below the camera, within immediate arm's reach and just above the wearer's right leg). Using the RGB strip for context, the scene contains the camera wearer's lower body and hands at the bottom of frames 1–4 (0.3–1.5 m away) facing forward toward the skateboard on the concrete floor (~1.5 m away), followed in frame 5 by a second person on the left (~0.6–1.4 m away, within arm's reach of the wearer and ~0.8 m from the wearer's feet) whose upper body and head are partly out of view at the left edge and who faces away from the camera wearer. When active in frame 3, the magenta keypoints clarify the exact finger and wrist articulation of the wearer's right hand against the similarly toned concrete background better than the motion-blurred RGB image alone. However, the pose map is severely unreliable throughout the sequence, completely failing to detect the camera wearer's hands in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, missing all body skeletons for the self-occluded, top-down view of the camera wearer across all frames, and missing the partially cropped second person and their outstretched left arm in frame 5.
